events.text: GM said they were still looking for players
Anthony told GM to finish Kibwe
Acomhal, a trade hub in the Eel Sea where many species and factions compete for trade, was introduced.
Gloine Mhargadh, the Glass Market, was described as the richest faction, speaking through Ciarán, a Moth-Person.
Na hIarannaigh, the Iron Ones, were described as the city's machine-keepers, speaking through Aisling, a Beetle-Person.
Clann Deamhan, the Demon Clan, was described as proud, protective of its enclave, and speaking through Tómas, a Flame-Deamhan.
Comhairle Acomhal, the Council, was described as slow to act, with Peadar, a Turtle-Person, sitting on it.
An Crosbhealach was described as a place where rivals sit at the same tables and outside conflicts stay outside.
The GM described the Eel Sea and the Glass Eel, custodian of reality that judges none of it.
A Glass Elver followed the party, serving the Eel of the Delta, and the party was asked which channel to choose.
Caravans and ships from a dozen worlds arrived at once at the Junction, and their cargo spilled into the streets.
Glass Market couriers carried crates of Vitreous under armed guard.
Iron Ones mechanics walked the loading cranes, tightening bolts.
An Fás traders sold baskets of fruit that were still growing, while Shopkeepers called out ever-lower prices.
The Council's bell rang the hour, and nobody looked up.
The party's location in Acomhal was named as the Junction.
